structured: Define agroforestry.
The practice of deliberately growing trees or shrubs together with crops and/or livestock on the same land. (2)
State four environmental benefits of agroforestry trees.
Reduce soil erosion, provide shade, improve biodiversity, act as windbreaks, add organic matter, conserve water/carbon. Any four.
Name three planting materials used to establish agroforestry trees.
Seeds, seedlings, stem cuttings, root suckers or other suitable vegetative materials. Any three.
Name three structures used to conserve surface runoff.
Terraces, contour bunds, water-retention pits, infiltration ditches, check dams. Any three.
State four practices used when caring for established agroforestry trees.
Watering, mulching, weeding, pruning, protecting from livestock/pests, applying manure. Any four.
Give four sites where crops may be planted.
Seedbeds, fields/gardens, containers, raised beds, ridges or planting holes. Any four appropriate sites.
Define soil tilth.
The physical condition or state of soil in relation to its suitability for cultivation and plant growth. (2)
Name three categories of soil tilth according to planting material size.
Fine, medium and coarse tilth. (1 each)
Describe three steps in preparing a ground seedbed.
Clear vegetation/debris; dig or loosen soil; break clods and level/rake to a suitable tilth. (1 each)
Give two main categories of planting materials.
Sexual materials (seeds) and vegetative/asexual materials. (1 each)
Name three vegetative planting materials.
Stem cuttings, root cuttings, suckers, tubers, bulbs, rhizomes. Any three.
State three methods of planting crops.
Broadcasting, drilling/row planting, dibbling, transplanting. Any three.
Give one way of predicting the time of planting.
Use weather forecasts/seasonal rainfall information or observe reliable local rainfall patterns. (2)
State two factors that determine time of planting.
Onset and reliability of rains, soil moisture, crop type, temperature, availability of water or market timing. Any two explained.
State four roles of Home Science education.
Promotes healthy living, food/nutrition knowledge, home management, budgeting/resource use, hygiene and safety, family relationships. Any four.
Give three guidelines for cooking food by roasting.
Prepare food appropriately; use moderate, even heat; turn food as needed; cook thoroughly; avoid charring. Any three.
State three safety measures when roasting food.
Use suitable tools/oven mitts; keep flammable items away; supervise fire/heat; use stable equipment; avoid touching hot surfaces. Any three.
State four factors to consider when buying household goods and services.
Price, quality, durability, need, safety, quantity, warranty, availability and seller reliability. Any four.
Differentiate between reusing and recycling and give one example of each.
Reuse means using an item again without major processing (1), e.g. jar as storage (1); recycling processes waste into new material/product (1), e.g. paper into new paper (1).
Explain two reasons for improvising food-preparation equipment.
Makes cooking possible when standard equipment is unavailable; reduces cost; encourages creativity and resource use. Any two explained.
Name four outlets where household goods and services may be obtained.
Supermarkets, shops, markets, wholesalers, online stores, cooperatives. Any four.
State four methods of buying household goods and services.
Cash purchase, hire purchase, credit, lay-by, online purchase, instalment payment. Any four.
Give five ways of saving income when buying household goods.
Prepare a budget, compare prices, buy only needed items, use shopping lists, buy durable goods, avoid impulse buying, take advantage of genuine discounts. Any five.
State five challenges people may face when buying household goods and services.
High prices, counterfeit goods, poor quality, shortages, misleading advertising, transport costs, price changes, limited access. Any five.
State three properties of cotton fibre.
Soft, absorbent, breathable, comfortable, washable and strong when wet. Any three.
Explain four ways trees in an agroforestry system can improve the farm environment.
Reduce soil erosion; provide shade/windbreaks; add organic matter; support biodiversity; improve water infiltration. Any four explained.
Describe how to establish a tree seedling in a prepared planting hole.
Select healthy seedling; prepare suitable hole; remove container carefully; place upright at correct depth; refill and firm soil; water and mulch. Award up to 5.
State four reasons for watering newly planted seedlings.
Helps roots establish; prevents wilting; supports nutrient uptake; maintains moisture during dry periods. Any four.
Give four signs that a seedbed is poorly prepared.
Large clods; stones and rubbish; uneven surface; compacted soil; poor drainage; excessive weeds. Any four.
Describe three differences between broadcasting and drilling seeds.
Broadcasting scatters seed over an area; drilling places seed in rows; drilling gives more uniform spacing/depth and easier weeding. Any three contrasts.
Explain four effects of weeds on crop growth.
Compete for nutrients, water, light and space; harbour pests/diseases; interfere with harvesting; reduce crop yield. Any four.
State four precautions when using hand tools for weeding.
Use correct tool; wear protective footwear/gloves; maintain safe distance; carry tools carefully; store after use. Any four.
Name four factors that influence the choice of a crop planting method.
Crop type/seed size; soil condition; land size; available labour/equipment; spacing needs; moisture. Any four.
Give four ways of conserving water on a farm.
Mulching, roof-water harvesting, water pans/tanks, contour structures, drip irrigation, repairing leaks. Any four.
Explain three reasons for using weather forecasts when planning planting.
Helps identify expected rainfall; reduces risk of planting into dry spells; assists timing of land preparation and crop establishment. Any three.
State four safe practices when roasting food.
Use clean equipment; control heat; keep children away from fire; use protective holders; cook thoroughly; avoid leaving fire unattended. Any four.
Explain four factors to consider when selecting household cooking equipment.
Safety, durability, cost, suitability, ease of cleaning, energy use, size and availability. Any four explained.
Describe four ways to prevent food contamination during preparation.
Wash hands; clean utensils/surfaces; separate raw and cooked foods; use safe water; cover food; store at safe temperatures. Any four.
State four causes of nutrient deficiency in a diet.
Limited food variety; poverty/food insecurity; illness or poor absorption; poor feeding practices; lack of nutrition knowledge. Any four.
Give one symptom and one prevention measure for iron-deficiency anaemia.
Symptoms: tiredness, pale skin, weakness or dizziness (1); prevention: iron-rich foods such as beans/green vegetables/meat and appropriate dietary vitamin C (1).
Explain the importance of reading labels when buying household goods.
Identify ingredients/materials; check instructions/warnings; compare quantity/price; check expiry/manufacturer details. Any four.
State four ways of avoiding waste when shopping for household goods.
Prepare list; budget; compare quantity and price; buy needed amounts; check quality/expiry; avoid impulse buying. Any four.
Differentiate between reuse and reduce, giving one example of each.
Reuse means use an item again (1) e.g. refill a suitable jar (1); reduce means use fewer resources/create less waste (1) e.g. avoid excess packaging (1).
State four safe ways of disposing of household waste.
Separate recyclables; compost suitable organic waste; use approved collection; safely contain hazardous waste; avoid dumping/burning plastics. Any four.
Describe four properties of cotton fibre that make it useful in clothing.
Soft, absorbent, breathable, comfortable, washable, takes dye and is reasonably strong. Any four.
Give four uses of cotton fibre or cotton fabric.
Clothing, towels, bedding, bandages, reusable bags, household textiles. Any four.
Explain three ways to care for cotton garments.
Wash appropriately; dry thoroughly; iron at suitable temperature; store clean and dry; treat stains promptly. Any three.
State four advantages of using locally available materials to improvise kitchen equipment.
Lower cost; readily available; reduces waste; encourages creativity; can be repaired/replaced easily. Any four.
Describe four considerations when choosing a sales outlet for household goods.
Price, quality, distance/accessibility, reputation, availability, return policy and safety. Any four.
Explain three reasons why a household should save part of its income.
Meet emergencies; plan future needs; reduce borrowing; finance education/assets. Any three.
Explain how contour farming conserves soil and water.
Cultivates across slope; slows runoff; increases infiltration; reduces erosion. Any four.
State four ways to prevent food wastage at home.
Plan meals; buy suitable quantities; store correctly; use leftovers safely; check expiry dates. Any four.
Explain why household income should be budgeted.
Prioritises needs; controls spending; supports saving; reduces debt; prepares for emergencies. Any four.
Give four safe practices when using a charcoal or wood stove.
Stable position; ventilation; keep children away; use suitable fuel; extinguish safely. Any four.
Give four ways of caring for young agroforestry trees.
Water; mulch; weed; protect from livestock; replace dead seedlings; prune appropriately. Any four.

structured: Define a 3D art form and give three examples.
A form with length, width and height (1); examples such as sculpture, pottery, carving, modelling. Any three (1 each).
Define still-life drawing.
A drawing of arranged non-living objects, such as fruits, utensils or bottles. (2)
Explain the meaning of composition in visual art.
The arrangement of visual elements in an artwork to create an organised and balanced whole. (2)
Define painting and name three tools/materials used.
Applying pigment/paint to a surface to create an image (2); brush, paint, palette, paper/canvas, water. Any three (1 each).
What is a colour wheel?
A circular arrangement of colours showing relationships among primary, secondary and related colours. (2)
Name the three primary colours in the traditional pigment model.
Red, yellow and blue. (1 each)
Give three pairs of analogous colours.
Red/orange, yellow/orange, yellow/green, blue/green, blue/violet, red/violet. Any three adjacent pairs.
Name the three basic properties of colour.
Hue, value and intensity/saturation. (1 each)
Define perspective in drawing.
A technique for representing three-dimensional depth and distance on a two-dimensional surface. (2)
Name three components or elements used when constructing perspective.
Horizon line, vanishing point and orthogonal/receding lines. (1 each)
Explain tint and shade.
Tint is made by adding white to a colour; shade is made by adding black. (1 each)
Describe how to create an intensity scale using orange paint.

Mix red and yellow to make orange; progressively alter the mixture with its complement/neutralising colour or controlled pigment addition to show stronger to duller intensity. Award for safe, logical graduated procedure. (3)
Explain how to make a colour gradation strip from red to yellow.
Prepare red and yellow; mix successive proportions in steps; paint adjacent bands showing gradual transition through orange. (3)
Define passing and reception in ball games.
Passing is sending the ball to a teammate (1); reception is receiving/controlling a ball from another player (1).
Define pivoting and marking in games.
Pivoting is turning on a planted foot while maintaining control (1); marking is guarding/opposing a player to limit their movement or options (1).
Name two types of passes used in handball.
Overarm/shoulder pass, bounce pass, chest pass, wrist pass. Any two.
State the dimensions of a standard handball court.
From what distance is a handball penalty throw taken?
7 metres from the goal. (1)
State two landing techniques used in netball footwork.
One-foot landing and two-foot landing. (1 each)
How many players from each team play on a netball court?
Seven players. (1)
State the time limit for a netball player to pass or shoot after receiving the ball.
Three seconds. (1)
Give four ways dancers can remain safe during a performance.
Warm up, clear the stage, wear suitable footwear/costume, check props, follow instructions, avoid unsafe lifts. Any four.
Name two activities dancers should do before a stage performance.
Warm-up/stretching and rehearsal; checking costume/props or stage positions also acceptable. Any two.
Name two materials used to make a sisal skirt.
Sisal fibre and string/thread; suitable waistband or binding material also accepted. (1 each)
Explain how a whistle and a guitar produce sound.
Whistle: blown air vibrates (1); guitar: plucked/strummed strings vibrate (1).
Explain four ways to create a sense of depth in a still-life drawing.
Use overlapping; vary size; place nearer objects lower/larger; use perspective; apply shading and tonal contrast. Any four explained.
State four principles to consider when composing a visual artwork.
Balance, proportion, emphasis, rhythm, unity, contrast and movement. Any four.
Describe how to create a smooth tonal scale using a pencil.
Draw a strip; shade from light to dark using gradual pressure; blend carefully; maintain even transitions. Award up to 4.
Explain the difference between a tint, shade and tone.
Tint adds white; shade adds black; tone is produced by adding grey or modifying intensity. (1 each)
Name four secondary or tertiary colours and explain how one is mixed.
Examples: orange, green, violet; tertiary examples such as red-orange or blue-green. Explain one valid mixture. Award up to 4.
State four ways perspective can make a drawing appear realistic.
Parallel lines appear to converge; distant objects look smaller; overlapping shows position; reduced detail/contrast suggests distance. Any four.
Give four safety measures when using paints and art tools.
Use materials as instructed; avoid ingestion/contact with eyes; ventilate area; clean spills; store sharp tools safely; wash hands. Any four.
Describe four stages in preparing a still-life composition.
Select objects; arrange them; observe viewpoint/light; sketch outlines; refine proportion; shade/colour. Any four in sequence.
Explain the difference between chest, bounce, shoulder and overhead passes in ball games.
Describe direction/technique of any four passes accurately. (1 each)
State four skills needed for effective netball reception.
Watch ball; move into position; extend hands; cushion/control ball; maintain balance; communicate. Any four.
Explain the purpose of pivoting in netball.
Allows a player to turn on a landing foot to find a teammate or passing space without committing a footwork infringement. Award up to 2.
State four examples of footwork or movement infringements in netball.
Moving/dragging landing foot illegally; hopping; stepping again before releasing ball; lifting pivot foot contrary to rules. Any four acceptable descriptions.
Give four differences between netball and handball.
Number of players, court/goal design, ball handling and dribbling rules, scoring method, positions/area restrictions. Any four valid contrasts.
Describe four ways a team can defend effectively in handball.
Mark attackers; block passing lanes; maintain defensive formation; communicate; track players; intercept passes safely. Any four.
State four preparations before a dance performance.
Rehearse; warm up; check costume/props; inspect stage; agree formations/cues; hydrate. Any four.
Explain four functions of a soloist in a group song.
Leads a verse/line; introduces melody; gives cues; sings a featured part; supports audience engagement. Any four.
Name four percussion instruments and state how each produces sound.
Drum—struck membrane; shaker—shaken contents; xylophone—struck bars; tambourine—shaken/struck jingles. Any four pairs.
Explain the function of a resonator in a drum.
It helps amplify and enrich the sound produced by the vibrating drum membrane. (2)
Write the French rhythm names for quaver, crotchet, minim and semibreve as taught in music notation.
Accept the curriculum-taught French rhythm syllables/names for each note value. Award one per correct response; verify against the class notation convention.
Describe how a guitar produces sound and how the sound is made louder.
Plucked/strummed strings vibrate (1); sound box/resonator amplifies the vibrations (1).
State four ways performers can show good stage etiquette.
Enter/exit on cue; respect other performers; avoid blocking views; handle props carefully; remain quiet offstage. Any four.
Explain four ways to avoid injury during dance practice.
Warm up; use safe floor; wear suitable footwear; maintain spacing; use correct technique; avoid unsafe lifts. Any four.
Describe how to make a simple sisal skirt safely.
Prepare sisal fibres; measure and prepare waistband; attach fibres evenly; secure knots/stitches; trim and check fit. Award up to 4.
Explain the difference between rhythm and tempo.
Rhythm is the pattern of sounds and silences (1); tempo is the speed of the beat (1).
State four roles of music in a community.
Entertainment, worship, education, communication, ceremonies, cultural preservation and unity. Any four.
Explain four ways artists can show texture in a drawing.
Hatching, cross-hatching, stippling, rubbing, varied line patterns and shading. Any four.
State four safety rules when practising games.
Warm up; safe surface; suitable footwear; follow rules; safe equipment; hydrate. Any four.
Describe how to receive a chest pass.
Watch ball; move into line; extend hands; cushion ball; maintain balance. Award up to 4.
Give four preparations before a stage presentation.
Rehearse; check costume/props; warm up; inspect stage; learn cues; arrange formation. Any four.
Explain the role of rhythm in dance.
Organises movement in time with beat, supports coordination and creates patterns. Award up to 3.

mcq: Which statement is a similarity between the biblical creation account and many African creation stories?
A supreme creator is responsible for the origin of life
The world made itself without any cause
Both traditions commonly describe a supreme creator as the source of creation.
According to Genesis 1, what did God create on the first day?
Genesis 1 describes the creation of light on the first day.
What was created on the second day in the first biblical creation account?
The second day describes the expanse separating waters.
Which creation work is associated with the third day in Genesis 1?
The third day describes dry land, seas and plants.
What was created on the fourth day according to Genesis 1?
The heavenly lights are appointed on the fourth day.
Which creatures were created on the fifth day in Genesis 1?
The fifth day includes creatures of the waters and birds.
Which creation work is associated with the sixth day?
Genesis 1 places land animals and human beings on the sixth day.
What did God do on the seventh day in the first creation account?
The seventh day is described as a day of rest and blessing.
Which book contains the two biblical creation accounts studied in Grade 7 CRE?
The creation accounts are found in Genesis.
Which reference gives the second biblical creation account in the source paper?
The supplied assessment specifically identifies Genesis 2:4–25.
In Genesis 2, what was formed from the dust of the ground?
Genesis 2 describes God forming the man from the dust of the ground.
According to Genesis 2, what did God do after forming the man from dust?
Sent him to build a city
Breathed into his nostrils the breath of life
The account says God breathed the breath of life into the man.
What was the name of the garden where God placed the man in Genesis 2?
What was the man instructed to do in the Garden of Eden?
Work it and take care of it
The man was placed in the garden to work it and care for it.
What was created as a companion for the man in Genesis 2?
The account describes the creation of the woman as a companion.
Which attribute of God is shown by creation of the world?
Which attribute of God is reflected in providing plants and food for living things?
Providing for living things reflects care and provision.
Which statement best expresses the Christian belief that God is eternal?
God has no beginning or end
Eternal means without beginning or end.
Why do Christians care for animals, fish and birds?
They should all be kept as pets
They are part of God's creation and should be treated responsibly
They are only useful for entertainment
Christians understand living creatures as part of God's creation and a trust to care for.
Which action shows care for birds?
Providing safe nesting places and protecting habitats
Protecting habitats and nests helps birds survive.
Avoiding pollution of rivers and lakes
Clean water is essential for aquatic life.
Providing clean water, food and shelter
Responsible care includes food, water, shelter and humane treatment.
Which is a likely effect of misusing natural resources?
Misuse can damage land and ecosystems, including through soil erosion.
How can cutting trees carelessly affect the environment?
It can cause soil erosion and loss of habitats
Tree removal can expose soil and destroy habitats.
Which action is an example of sustainable use of natural resources?
Planting trees to replace those cut down
Replanting trees helps maintain resources for future generations.
Which is an appropriate use of the Bible during worship?
Reading passages and guiding prayers or teaching
Replacing all school books with it
The Bible is read and used for teaching and worship.
How may the Bible be used during a Christian wedding?
Scripture may be read to guide and bless the marriage ceremony.
How can the Bible be used when visiting a sick person?
Reading encouraging passages and offering comfort
Bible passages may provide spiritual encouragement and comfort.
How many books are in the Protestant Old Testament?
The Protestant Old Testament contains 39 books.
How many books are in the Protestant New Testament?
How many books are in the Protestant Bible altogether?
The Protestant Bible has 39 Old Testament and 27 New Testament books.
Which of the following is one of the major prophets?
Isaiah is traditionally grouped among the major prophets.
Which list contains books traditionally associated with the major prophets?
Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel and Daniel
Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy
