structured: Name three components of Social Studies.
Geography, History, Civics/Government, Economics or related social sciences. Any three (1 each).
Name the four main internal layers/regions of the Earth commonly shown in a cross-section.
Crust, mantle, outer core and inner core. (1 each)
Distinguish between rotation and revolution of the Earth.
Rotation is spinning on its axis (1); revolution is movement around the Sun along an orbit (1).
State two effects of Earth's rotation and two effects of its revolution.
Rotation: day/night and apparent movement of sun/stars or time differences (any two); revolution: year and seasonal changes when combined with axial tilt (any two).
Name three weather-measuring instruments and state what each measures.
Thermometer—temperature; rain gauge—rainfall; wind vane—wind direction; anemometer—wind speed; barometer—air pressure; hygrometer—humidity. Any three pairs.
Give one example of a community from each group: Bantu, Nilotes, Cushites, Europeans and Asians.
Examples: Bantu—Kikuyu/Luhya/Kamba; Nilotes—Luo/Maasai/Kalenjin; Cushites—Somali/Rendille; Europeans—British/French; Asians—Indian/Chinese. One each.
Define population and population density.
Population is the total number of people in an area (1); population density is the number of people per unit area (1).
Name the Kenyan localities associated with soda ash, fluorspar and diatomite.
Soda ash—Lake Magadi; fluorspar—Kerio Valley; diatomite—Kariandusi/Gilgil. (1 each)
State two factors to consider when siting a weather station.
Open level ground; away from buildings/trees; secure and accessible; representative of local conditions. Any two.
Differentiate between densely and sparsely populated areas.
Densely populated areas have many people per unit area; sparsely populated areas have few people per unit area. (2)
Define culture and give two aspects of culture.
Culture is a community's way of life (1); language, food, dress, beliefs, customs, music, dance or ceremonies. Any two (1 each).
What is cultural heritage? Give three examples of places or institutions that preserve it.
Inherited cultural/historical features and practices (1); museums, monuments, historic buildings, cultural centres. Any three (1 each).
State three elements of weather.
Temperature, rainfall, wind, humidity, air pressure, cloud cover. Any three.
What are monuments and why are they important?
Structures/statues commemorating people or events (1); preserve memory/history and educate future generations (1).
Name the capital cities of Burundi and Morocco.
Burundi—Gitega; Morocco—Rabat. (1 each)
State three facts about planet Earth.
Third planet from the Sun; supports known life; has liquid water; approximately spherical; has one natural moon. Any three.
On which two dates is the Sun overhead at the Equator during the equinoxes?
Around 20/21 March and 22/23 September. (1 each)
Name three main components/gases of the atmosphere.
Nitrogen, oxygen and argon/carbon dioxide/water vapour. Any three valid constituents.
Define horticulture.
The growing of fruits, vegetables, flowers and ornamental plants. (1)
Name three important lines of latitude crossing or near Africa.
Equator, Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn. (1 each)
Explain how to calculate local time using longitude.
Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours, so 15° = 1 hour and 1° = 4 minutes; add time eastward and subtract westward. (3)
Freetown is at 15°W and it is 7:00 a.m. What is the local time at Cape Town, 18°E? Show working.
Longitude difference = 33° (1); time difference = 33×4 = 132 min = 2 h 12 min (1); Cape Town is east, add: 9:12 a.m. (1).
State three importance of maps in everyday life.
Locating places, route planning/navigation, showing distribution of features, planning development, studying regions. Any three.
Name three components of the solar system.
Sun, planets, moons, asteroids, comets, meteoroids. Any three.
Name the planets referred to as the Red Planet, Evening Star, largest planet and ringed planet.
Mars; Venus; Jupiter; Saturn. (1 each)
Name two theories that have been used to explain the origin of the solar system.
Nebular hypothesis and planetesimal/tidal hypothesis. (1 each)
Outline the nebular hypothesis of the origin of the solar system.

A rotating cloud of gas and dust contracted under gravity; the central mass formed the Sun; remaining material flattened into a disc and accreted to form planets and other bodies. Award up to 5 for ordered points.
Give three names used to describe the Earth's shape.
Spherical, oblate spheroid, geoid. (1 each)
State three pieces of evidence that the Earth is approximately spherical.
Ships disappear hull-first over horizon; circular shadow during lunar eclipse; circumnavigation; photographs from space; changing stars with latitude. Any three.
State four effects of Earth's rotation on human activities.
Creates day/night cycle; causes differences in local time; influences daily work/rest schedules; apparent movement of Sun affects timing of activities. Any four explained.
State four elements of weather.
Temperature, rainfall, wind, humidity, cloud cover and air pressure. Any four.
Explain four effects of Earth's rotation.
Day and night; apparent movement of sun; local time differences; deflection of winds/currents. Any four.
State four reasons maps are useful.
Show locations; routes; estimate distance; display physical/human features; support planning. Any four.
Name four weather instruments and what each measures.
Thermometer—temperature; rain gauge—rainfall; wind vane—direction; anemometer—wind speed; barometer—pressure. Any four.
Differentiate latitude and longitude.
Latitude measures angular distance north/south of Equator (2); longitude measures east/west of Prime Meridian (2).
